title: RAG is dead, right?? — Kuba Rogut, Turbopuffer
talk_summary: Kuba Rogut argues 'RAG is dead' is misleading: retrieval is broadening from one-shot vector search to hybrid, iterative, tool-rich agentic search (vector + BM25 + grep/glob/regex + filters). He contrasts per-session grep discovery (Claude Code) with pre-indexed semantic search (Cursor), framing embeddings as cached compute that trades upfront indexing cost for cheaper, faster runtime retrieval.

takeaways.technique: Pre-index codebase instead of per-session grep discovery
takeaways.what_they_do: Cursor parses/chunks/embeds a codebase once, then agents query a lightweight semantic tool at runtime instead of re-grepping and re-reading files every session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's this upfront cost of indexing but then we're able to allow for this like lightweight tool to help the agent kind of retrieve this information at runtime
takeaways.numbers: ~12.5-13.5% answer-accuracy gain across models; ~24% for composer; 2.6% code retention, 2.2% fewer dissatisfied requests in A/B

takeaways.what_they_do: Amortize a one-time parse/embed cost so repeated identical questions across agents/days don't re-derive the same understanding via grep-read loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: embeddings and semantic search are kind of cash compute
takeaways.numbers: 6,000 tokens cited as cost of one grep-read sub-step

takeaways.what_they_do: Hash-tree comparison between similar codebases lets them copy prior index and only re-chunk/re-embed changed files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use like Merkle trees ... calculate similarities between code bases ... only update the ... re-chunk and re-embed the files that have changed

takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents multiple retrieval tools (vector, BM25 full-text, grep/glob, regex, filters) and let them iterate and pick per query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: retrieval is not just vector search. It's a lot of different things ... BM25, grepping, globbing, using regex

takeaways.technique: Retrieve the right slice, not the biggest window
takeaways.what_they_do: Narrow huge corpora down to the relevant ~10k-1M tokens before passing to the model, rather than stuffing a giant context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need a trillion at once, you need the right million
